title: Workflow from runbook
description: Turn a written procedure into a tested workflow definition with a dry-run ledger check.

steps.name: draft
steps.prompt: Read the runbook, SOP or notes you were given (file path or pasted text in the task). Draft a workflow definition as JSON matching WorkflowDef: 2 to 7 coarse steps, each with a prompt an agent can act on, connectors, intendedActions with scopes and caps, and a reviewer step. Save it to workflow.draft.json.

steps.name: dry-run
steps.prompt: Use the control plane API at $API_URL (curl is fine; JSON responses). Useful routes: GET /projects, GET /projects/:id, GET /sessions, GET /sessions/:id/events, GET /graph/:id, GET /workflows, GET /workflows/:id, GET /brief?hours=N, GET /audit?limit=N, GET /chores, GET /ledgers?status=signed, GET /proposals, POST /workflows, POST /projects, POST /projects/:id/continue, POST /chores, POST /tasks/:id/go. POST the draft to /workflows, create a task with scheduledFor tomorrow 22:00 via /projects/:id/continue or /tasks, then POST /ledgers/generate for it and read the ledger. Any action listed under neverPreAuthorised must be deliberately placed on a step that expects to park. Fix the draft and re-post until the ledger is what you intend. Write ledger.review.md explaining each grant.

steps.name: review
steps.prompt: Review workflow.draft.json and ledger.review.md: are the scopes tight, are the caps realistic, is anything outward missing a park? Report only.
